newsitem.title: MEXICO: Analysts say Mexico March inflation favorable.
newsitem.headline: Analysts say Mexico March inflation favorable.

text.p: Analysts said on Wednesday that Mexico's March inflation, reported at 1.24 percent, was a favorable number that should help interest rates remain stable.
"It is a favorable number," AB Asesores Moneda head of analysis Diego Bravo said.
Said Interacciones chief economist Alonso Cervera: "The adjustment in inflation has been better than we expected."
A survey of economists by Reuters had forecast March inflation at an average 1.31 percent.
Economists had been forecasting inflation would decelerate after hitting a recent peak of 2.57 percent in January, which slowed to 1.68 percent in February.
"We believed the trend was downward," Bravo said.
Banco de Mexico said the cumulative inflation rate for the first three months of the year was 5.59 percent, compared with 8.35 percent in the same period a year ago.
"The current numbers are very encouraging and we are expecting the annual inflation rate to reach about 17.0 percent," Cervera said.
"Interest rates should benefit from this lower-than-expected inflation scenario. However, there are still those concerns regarding the elections," he said.
Mexico will hold key mid-term elections on July 6 this year, which could see support for the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party weaken, according to opinion polls.
"You could have inflation going down, but at the same time investors demanding a higher real premium in pesos. Nominal rate then will not go down that much," he said.
He said the benchmark one-month Cetes rate will likely fluctuate between 18.0 percent and 22.0 percent for the rest of the year.
At the weekly Cetes auction on Tuesday, one-month Treasury bills yielded 22.33 percent.
"Some players were hoping for an even lower level, but markets should react calmly to this level," MMS International wrote in a market report about the inflation number.
In March, the producer price index, excluding petroleum, was 0.97 percent higher than the same month a year earlier, it said.
